harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Published node2's HTTP service (port 8080) on node1's (OPNsense) LAN address port 80 via a port-forward with NAT reflection (Pure NAT), plus a manual outbound source-NAT rule so hairpinned traffic to node2 arrives sourced as node1's own IP. node2's firewalld only accepts port 8080 from node1's address, forcing node3 to reach the service through http://10.100.9.10:80/ rather than hitting node2:8080 directly (which is rejected). All three nodes were then restarted one at a time per the mandatory protocol, with boot-identity changes confirmed and full service/NAT/firewall recovery verified after each.
actions_performed: Surveyed topology: node1=OPNsense (single LAN interface 10.100.9.10/24, no separate WAN interface configured), node2/node3=RHEL9 on the same 10.100.9.0/24 subnet
Created a persistent systemd service (simplehttp.service, python3 http.server) on node2 serving 'hello from node2:8080' on TCP 8080
Configured firewalld on node2 with priority rich rules: accept tcp/8080 only from source 10.100.9.10 (node1), reject tcp/8080 from all other sources

Edited /conf/config.xml on node1: added a DNAT/port-forward rule (lan interface, dest port 80 -> target 10.100.9.11 port 8080, natreflection=purenat), disabled the webGUI's own HTTP redirect listener on port 80 (system/webgui/disablehttpredirect) since it was intercepting port 80 ahead of the port-forward, added a filter pass rule for the forwarded traffic, and added a manual outbound NAT rule (mode=hybrid) that source-NATs LAN traffic destined to 10.100.9.11:8080 to node1's own LAN IP so the hairpinned connection works despite node2 firewalld's source restriction

Applied changes via configctl filter reload; verified via pfctl -s nat and pfctl -s state that the rdr and outbound SNAT rules were active and that node2 observed connections sourced as 10.100.9.10, not node3's real IP
Verified end-to-end from node3: curl http://10.100.9.10:80/ returns the node2 service payload; direct curl from node3 to node2:8080 is rejected (curl exit 7 / http_code 000)
Captured healthy boot-identity baselines on all 3 nodes (node1 kern.boottime, node2/node3 /proc/sys/kernel/random/boot_id) plus proof of working service/NAT before touching any node

Restarted node2 via 'shutdown -r now' (backgrounded so ack returned before disconnect); polled until reachable; confirmed boot_id changed (67c52137... -> 0a755b07...); verified simplehttp.service active, firewalld rich rules persisted, and hairpin path still worked from node3

Restarted node1 (OPNsense) via 'shutdown -r now'; polled until reachable; confirmed kern.boottime changed (1788629109 -> 1788629562); verified pf nat/rdr/outbound-SNAT rules persisted from config.xml and reapplied on boot, and hairpin path worked from node3

Restarted node3 via 'shutdown -r now'; polled until reachable; confirmed boot_id changed (910dc564... -> 727fb5aa...); verified it could still reach the service via http://10.100.9.10:80/ and that direct access to node2:8080 remained blocked

evidence.requirement: node2 HTTP service on port 8080 exists and is healthy
evidence.summary: systemd unit simplehttp.service created and confirmed active, listening on 0.0.0.0:8080, curl to 127.0.0.1:8080 returns payload

evidence.requirement: Service published on TCP port 80 of node1's outward-facing (LAN) address via NAT reflection/hairpin
evidence.summary: config.xml edited to add DNAT port-forward (80->10.100.9.11:8080, purenat reflection), disable conflicting webGUI redirect on port 80, and add manual outbound source-NAT rule; pfctl -s nat confirms both the rdr and the new source-nat rule are active

evidence.requirement: node3 reaches the service through node1's address (not node2 directly)
evidence.summary: curl from node3 to http://10.100.9.10:80/ returns 'hello from node2:8080' repeatably; direct curl from node3 to node2:8080 fails (000); pf state table shows node2 sees the connection sourced as node1's IP (10.100.9.10), confirming true hairpin/source translation

evidence.requirement: node2 does not accept the service port directly from node3
evidence.summary: firewalld rich rules on node2 accept tcp/8080 only from 10.100.9.10 and reject from all other sources; verified node3 direct access is rejected

evidence.requirement: Healthy baseline captured before any restarts (all nodes)
evidence.summary: Captured kern.boottime (node1) and /proc/sys/kernel/random/boot_id (node2, node3) plus service-active status prior to any restart

evidence.requirement: node2 restart: acknowledgement, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: shutdown -r now acked before disconnect; boot_id changed from 67c52137... to 0a755b07...; simplehttp.service active, firewalld rules intact, hairpin path from node3 works post-restart

evidence.requirement: node1 (OPNsense) restart: acknowledgement, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: shutdown -r now acked before disconnect; kern.boottime changed from sec=1788629109 to sec=1788629562; pf nat/rdr/outbound-SNAT rules persisted and reloaded from config.xml; node3 hairpin access and direct-block both confirmed post-restart

evidence.summary: shutdown -r now acked before disconnect; boot_id changed from 910dc564... to 727fb5aa...; post-restart curl confirms hairpin access to node1:80 works and direct node2:8080 access remains blocked
